speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your condition, could you describe the specific nature and location of your flank pain and whether you are experiencing any pain or burning during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty passing urine, such as frequent urges, urgency, or seeing blood in your urine? I also need to know if you have any nausea, vomiting, or chills accompanying your fever.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the rash appear only on your skin, or did you notice any swelling of your face or lips? I also need to know if you have experienced any changes in urine output or seen blood in your urine since starting the cephalexin.

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rash following antibiotic use and persistent fever despite resolved sinusitis, I suspect a drug-induced interstitial nephritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_with_Sediment.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in the urine sediment strongly supports a diagnosis of acute interstitial nephritis likely triggered by the antibiotics. To confirm the extent of renal involvement, I need to assess your kidney function. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine_and_BUN.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatinine and BUN confirm acute kidney injury, which, combined with the urinary eosinophils and recent antibiotic exposure, strongly points to acute interstitial nephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
